verse: Do not exalt yourself, or else you might fall and bring dishonor to your soul. The Lord will reveal your secrets, and he will overthrow you in front of everyone, because you did not come in the fear of the Lord, and your heart was full of deceit. (Sir 1:30)
The beginning of the pride of man is to forsake the Lord. (Sir 10:12)
The heart has withdrawn from the one who made him. For pride is the beginning of all sin. (Sir 10:12-13)
Pride goes before destruction and a haughty spirit before a fall. (Pro 16:18)
The loftiness of men will be bowed down, and the haughtiness of men will be brought low. And the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day. (Is 2:17)
The heart of a man is haughty before it is crushed and humbled before it is glorified. (Pro 18:12)
If anyone considers himself to be something, though he may be nothing, he deceives himself. (Gal 6:3)
Do you see a man who is wise in his own eyes? There is more hope for a fool than for him. (Pro 26:12)
A person's pride shall bring him low: but honor shall uphold the humble in spirit. (Pro 29:23)
Live in harmony with one another. Do not be haughty, but associate with the lowly. Do not be wise in your own sight. (Rom 12:16)
Every proud man is an abomination to the Lord; they surely won’t go unpunished. (Pro 16:5)
Let the one who boasts, boast in the Lord. For it is not the one who commends himself who is approved, but the one whom the Lord commends. (2 Cor 10:17-18)
When his heart was lifted up and his spirit was hardened so that he dealt proudly, he was brought down from his kingly throne, and his glory was taken from him. (Dan 5:20)
The Lord will destroy the house of the proud, but he sets the widow’s boundary stones in place. (Pro 15:25)
I will punish the world for its evil, and the wicked for their iniquity; and I will cause the arrogancy of the proud to cease and will lay low the haughtiness of the tyrants. (Is 13:11)
The pride of your heart has deceived you, you that dwell in the clefts of the rock, whose dwelling is in the heights; you said in your heart, who shall bring me down to the ground? (Obad 1:3)
You boast in your arrogance: all such boasting is evil. (Jas 4:16)

These six things the Lord hates: seven that are an abomination to him: A proud look, a lying tongue, and hands that shed innocent blood, The heart that devises wicked plans, feet that hurry in running to evil, a false witness that speak lies, and he who sows discord among brethren. (Pro 6:16-19)
Haughty eyes, a proud heart, and the lamp of the wicked are sin. (Pro 21:4)
The Lord lifts up the meek, he casts the wicked down to the ground. (Ps 147:6)
Blessed are the meek, for they shall inherit the earth. (Matt 5:5)
Seek the Lord, all you meek of the earth, who obey his commands. Seek righteousness, seek humility: if may be that you may be hidden on the day of the Lord's anger. (Zeph 2:3)
For everyone who exalts himself shall be humbled, and whoever humbles himself shall be exalted. (Luk 14:11)
The wisdom of the humble people raises their heads high and sits them in the midst of the great. (Sir 11:1)
God chose what is lowly and despised in the world, even things that are not, to bring to nothing things that are, so that no human being might boast in the presence of God. (1 Cor 1:28-29)
The eyes of the arrogant will be humbled and human pride brought low; the Lord alone will be exalted in that day. (Is 2:11)
O mortal, what is good? and what does the Lord require of us, but to do what is just, and to love kindness, and to walk humbly with our God? (Mic 6:8)

He emptied himself, taking the form of a servant, being made in the likeness of humans, and accepting the human form. He humbled himself, becoming obedient unto death, even death on a Cross. (Phil 2:7-8)

If I then, your Lord and Teacher, have washed your feet, you also ought to wash the feet of one another. For I have given you an example, so that just as I have done for you, so also should you do. (Jn 13:14-15)
Humble your spirit greatly, for the godless will suffer the punishment of fire and worms. (Sir 7:17)
Whoever desires to become great among you shall be your servant; and whoever desires to be first among you shall be the slave of all. (Mrk 10:43-44)
The greatest among you shall be your servant. For those who exalt themselves will be humbled, and those who humble themselves will be exalted. (Matt 23:11-12)

This is said by the Most High, the Sublime one, who dwells in eternity. And his name is Holy, for he dwells in the exalted and holy place, and also with the contrite and humble spirit, to revive the spirit of the humble, and to revive the heart of the contrite. (Is 57:15)
He will direct the humble in what is right. He will teach the meek his ways. (Ps 25:9)
For you will deliver the humble people, but you will bring down the eyes of the arrogant. (Ps 18:27)
Yet truly, because he humbled himself, the wrath of the Lord turned away from him, so that he was not utterly destroyed. (2 Chron 12:12)
For, to the lowly, great mercy is granted, but the powerful will endure powerful torment. (Wis 6:6)

If my people, over whom my name has been invoked, humble themselves, and pray and seek my face and turn from their wicked ways, then I will heed them from heaven, and I will forgive their sins, and I will heal their land. (2 Chron 7:14)

Hear and pay attention; do not be proud, for the Lord has spoken. Give glory to the Lord your God, before darkness falls, and before your feet stumble on the darkened mountains. You will expect light, but he will turn it into the shadow of death and into utter darkness. (Jer 13:15-16)
The Lord is well pleased with his people, and he will exalt the humble unto salvation. (Ps 149:4)
When pride comes, disgrace follows; but wisdom is with the humble. (Pro 11:2)
Be humbled in the sight of the Lord, and he will exalt you. (Jas 4:10)
Be humbled under the powerful hand of God, so that he may exalt you in due time. (1 Pet 5:6)
Though the Lord is exalted, yet he looks with favor on the humble. But the proud he knows from a distance. (Ps 138:6)
The fruit of humility and the fear of the Lord is riches and glory and life. (Pro 22:4)
God resists the proud, but he gives grace to the humble. (Jas 4:6)
Perform your works in meekness, and you shall be loved by those accepted by God. The greater you become, the more humble you should be, and you will find grace in the presence of God. (Sir 3:17-18)
The prayer of one who humbles himself will pierce the clouds. And it will not be consoled till it reaches its goal; and it will not withdraw until the Most High responds. (Sir 35:21)

I say, through the grace that has been given to me, to all who are among you: not to think of yourself more highly than you ought to think, but think with sober judgement, each according to the measure of faith that God has apportioned. (Rom 12:3)
You humbled yourself before me, and you tore your clothes and wept before me, I also have heard you, says the Lord. (2 Chron 34:27)
